title: Approve the draft and find the story in the tree
prompt:
# Story 4: Approve the draft and find the story in the tree

- **Story**: XXX-approve-story
- **Created**: 2026-11-09
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: approve a ready draft, see the message with the card that opens the file, open `stories` in the tree, open the folder and then
  `story.md`, reload the page and find it all still there.

## Story

As a team member, I want to approve a draft so that it becomes a story of my project, in its own folder in the tree, so that my team can read
it and build it.

## Acceptance tests

Approving

- [ ] **Given** a Ready draft of a story, **Then** the card has "Discard" and "Approve and create story", which is enabled. **Given** any other
  state, **Then** "Approve and create story" is disabled.
- [ ] **Given** a Ready draft, **When** the user presses "Approve and create story", **Then** the story is stored with: id
  `001-as-a-returning-customer-i`, number, slug, title, the user's first prompt, today's date, the Markdown as drafted (trimmed, with one
  final newline), the links, and its tasks (below). It has no theme.
- [ ] **Given** the Markdown, **Then** the title is read from its first `# ` line with the prefixes "Story:", "Feature specification:" and
  "AE-<digits>." taken off. **Given** it has no such line, **Then** the title is made from the first sentence of the prompt, cut at 67
  characters and followed by "..." when it is longer than 70, with the first letter in capitals.
- [ ] **Given** approval, **Then** two messages are added: the user's prompt, and "Approved. I created the folder
  stories/001-as-a-returning-customer-i/ with story.md." (with " It is linked to 2 other items." when it has links; "1 other item" for
  one), with a card that shows `stories/001-as-a-returning-customer-i/story.md` and "Open file".
- [ ] **Given** approval, **Then** the draft is gone, the box is empty and not ticked, and the folders `stories` and
  `001-as-a-returning-customer-i` are open in the tree.
- [ ] **Given** a second approved story, **Then** its number is `002`, even when its first words are the same.

The tasks of the story

- [ ] **Given** the Markdown has a section `## Tasks`, **Then** the story is stored with one task for each item in it, in order. An item is a
  list line with no indent, bulleted (`-`, `*`, `+`) or numbered (`1.` or `1)`), with or without a checkbox. The list ends at a horizontal
  rule, at the next heading, or at the end of the text.
- [ ] **Given** a task that is only an empty box (`- [ ]`), or an item that is indented under another, **Then** it is not a task.
- [ ] **Given** two tasks with the same text (ignoring case, extra spaces and the ends), **Then** only the first is kept.
- [ ] **Given** the Markdown has no `## Tasks`, **Then** the story has no tasks.
- [ ] **Given** the stored tasks, **Then** each has its own id and its text, and the text of the story is not changed. (Showing the list, and
  adding or removing a task, are not here.)

The tree

- [ ] **Given** an approved story, **Then** the folder `stories` lists a folder named `001-as-a-returning-customer-i`, in order of number, with the
  count of the folder right, and opening it shows `story.md`, whose tooltip is `1. <title>`.
- [ ] **Given** no story, **Then** the open folder `stories` shows the italic line "No stories yet. Write a prompt." (it showed "Coming in another
  story." before this story).
- [ ] **Given** stories in themes, **Then** the tree is as `story-group-stories-by-theme.md` says. A story created here starts outside any
  theme, among the folders of `stories`.

Reading it

- [ ] **Given** the card in the conversation, or `story.md` in the tree, **When** the user presses it, **Then** the file opens in the same panel
  as an enabler, a driver or an ADR: the story icon, the path `stories/001-.../story.md`, Close, the two views (rendered and Markdown), the
  tree as a thin rail, and the prompt as a narrow column on the right.
- [ ] **Given** the open story, **Then** the panel says, with a lock, "Read-only here. Changing a story comes in another story." and has no Save,
  Delete, Sync, "Add task", diagram, UI example or "Add link" control. (`story-link-picker.md` adds the links; the stories that follow add the
  rest.)
- [ ] **Given** the open story, **Then** its links show under "Linked to" and what refers to it under "Referenced by", as `story-link-picker.md`
  says.

Discarding and keeping

- [ ] **Given** a draft is on screen, **When** the user presses "Discard", **Then** nothing is stored. **When** the user presses "New", **Then**
  the confirmation of story 1 asks first.
- [ ] **Given** the page is reloaded, **Then** the approved stories, their tasks, their links and the conversation are still there. **Given** two
  projects, **Then** each keeps its own.

## Business rules and constraints

- Only a Ready draft is approved. Approving is the user's decision: the AI never stores anything.
- The identity of a story is its folder name, `<number>-<slug>`, and the reference to it is `story:<number>-<slug>`. It comes from the name
  and never from a random id, so that a link means the same on every machine. It does not include a theme, so moving a story never breaks a link.
- The title is read from the document, so that it can be changed in the text later.
- The tasks of a story are copied **once**, from its `## Tasks`, when it is approved. They are the story's own list from then on.
- Everything is kept in the browser in the spike (`localStorage`, per project). The final storage is another decision.
- A story has no ADRs it derives from. An ADR it uses is an ordinary link.

## Out of scope

- Editing the story by hand or by prompt, its task list (showing, adding, removing and completing tasks), diagrams, the UI example, deleting,
  moving it into a theme, and synchronising it, which writes `stories/001-.../story.md`, `meta.json`, `ui.html` and the diagrams.
- Creating a story without the AI, and importing stories from the repository (they appear in the tree through the sync story).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `addStory` to the project's store: the story, its links and tasks, and the two messages, saved together.
- [ ] Read the title from the Markdown, with the fallback from the prompt.
- [ ] Read the tasks from `## Tasks` (the rules above) when the story is approved.
- [ ] Build the message with the card, and the text with the number of links.
- [ ] List the story folders in the tree in order of number, with `story.md` inside, the empty line and the count, and open `stories` and the new
  folder after approving.
- [ ] Open a story in the read-only panel with its note and no controls that edit.
- [ ] Test: approve, the title rules, the task rules (a list, numbers, empty boxes, indent, a rule, duplicates, none), the second number, the
  tree, reload, two projects and discard.

tasks.text: Add `addStory` to the project store: persist the story record, its links, its tasks, and the two approval messages together in `localStorage` (Architecture: infrastructure layer).

Implement title extraction from the first `# ` line of the Markdown, stripping "Story:", "Feature specification:", and "AE-`<digits>`." prefixes, with the prompt-sentence fallback (Architecture: use-case layer).

Implement task extraction from `## Tasks`: parse non-indented list items, skip empty checkboxes and indented items, stop at a horizontal rule or the next heading, and deduplicate by normalised text (Architecture: use-case layer).
Build the approval confirmation message and the "Open file" card, including the link-count suffix (Architecture: interface-adapter layer).
Enable "Approve and create story" only when the draft state is Ready; keep it disabled for all other states (Architecture: UI layer).

Update the `stories` folder in the tree: list story folders in number order, show `story.md` inside each, update the folder count, open `stories` and the new folder after approval, and replace the placeholder text with "No stories yet. Write a prompt." when empty (Architecture: UI layer).

Implement the read-only story file panel: story icon, path, Close, rendered and Markdown views, tree rail, prompt column, lock indicator with read-only message, and no editing controls (Architecture: UI layer).
Wire the "Open file" card in the conversation and the `story.md` node in the tree to open the read-only panel (Architecture: UI layer).

Write Jest tests covering: approval happy path, title extraction rules, task extraction rules (list styles, empty checkboxes, indented items, horizontal-rule termination, duplicates, no-Tasks section), second story numbering, tree state after approval, page-reload persistence, two-project isolation, and discard behaviour (Practice: Ten-Minute Build).
